# CoreWeave | Dynamo RL Rollouts Requirements

* **Author**: CoreWeave team  
* **Audience**: NVIDIA Dynamo team  
* **Security Tier**: Confidential

---

# 1\. Goal

CoreWeave is building managed inference support for **reinforcement learning (RL) post-training rollouts**, with NVIDIA Dynamo plus vLLM/Sglang as the serving stack. This document states what the workload needs end to end and the specific items we are asking NVIDIA to build (section 6). The user stories in section 4 give the full context.

**Target CoreWeave launch date:** **2026-09-25**, for demo at 2026 CoreWeave Fully Connected (September 29 to October 1, 2026). **Need all (NVIDIA) dependencies ready by 2026-09-15 for integration and validation.**

# 2\. Scope: the RL post-training loop

RL post-training runs a loop:

1. **Rollout generation.** The current policy revision v\_current serves inference requests and returns not just text but the **per-token training signal** the trainer needs (token IDs, logprobs, and for MoE models expert routing metadata).  
2. A reward function scores the responses; the trainer computes a weight update.  
3. A new policy revision v\_next is produced.  
4. **Weight synchronization.** v\_next is transferred into the running inference workers and made active.  
5. Periodically evaluate, check stopping criteria, then set v\_current \= v\_next and repeat.

**Steps 1 and 4 are both in scope for this document.** 

# 3\. Terminology

| Term | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Policy** | The LLM whose weights are being optimized. |
| **Rollout** | Generating responses from the current policy for scoring. Note this is the opposite of the usual infra meaning of "rollout". |
| **Experience** | The data a rollout returns to the trainer: token IDs, logprobs, rewards, and any auxiliary per-token metadata. |
| **Hot-load** | Loading new weights into a running inference process without restarting the process or its pod. |
| **Snapshot** | One checkpoint artifact, either full (complete weights) or incremental (a XOR-delta against a previous checkpoint). |
| **Snapshot chain** | An ordered list starting at a full baseline whose merged result is the target checkpoint. |
| **Identity** | The customer-chosen name of a snapshot, for example v3 or step-000420. The unit of readiness polling and of revision-aware routing. |
| **Trajectory** | One complete sampled path, that is, one response, or one full conversation in multi-turn RL. The unit of session affinity and of cache-salt scoping. |

# 4\. User stories

Written from the perspective of the RL trainer (an external orchestrator driving the loop) and of CoreWeave as the managed inference provider.

### 4.1 Rollout generation (step 1\)

1. As a trainer, I submit **token IDs rather than text**, so my tokenizer stays authoritative and the engine does not re-tokenize my input.   
2. As a trainer, I receive the generated **token IDs** back in the response, via the completion\_token\_ids response field.  
3. As a trainer, I receive the **logprob of every sampled completion token**, so I can compute importance-sampling ratios between the sampling policy and the training policy.  
4. As a trainer, I receive the **top-k alternative logprobs per token** (via the logprobs request parameter).  
5. As a trainer, I receive **prompt\_logprobs** for the input tokens.  
6. As a trainer doing MoE analysis, I receive **per-token expert routing metadata** so I can replay router decisions offline.  
7. As a trainer at large scale, the experience payload transfers **without dominating my loop time**. *(Ask, section 6.3.)*  
8. As a trainer, I pin every request in one **trajectory to the same replica**, so prefix cache reuse holds for multi-turn rollouts.

### 4.2 Weight synchronization (step 4\)

9. As a trainer, I publish a new checkpoint and **start a hot-load with one API call that returns immediately**, so my loop is never blocked on a multi-minute synchronous request.  
10. As a trainer, I **poll one status endpoint** and learn, per replica, which checkpoint identity is loaded and whether it is ready, so I know exactly when the next rollout round may begin.  
11. As a trainer, I upload a **zstd-compressed** full or delta checkpoint to object storage once; the first worker loads it, and the remaining workers pull full or delta weights **GPU-to-GPU from that peer over RDMA**, rather than repeating the object-storage transfer for every worker. *(Ask, section 6.1.)*  
12. As a trainer, I ship checkpoints at **training precision** and the serving engine **quantizes them during load** to the serving precision. *(Ask, section 6.2.)*  
13. As a trainer, I hot-load either a **full or incremental (XOR-delta) checkpoint**, so I can establish a new baseline when needed and use deltas between full checkpoints to reduce weight synchronization cost.  
14. As a trainer running **on-policy**, I wait until *all* replicas report the new identity before sending the next round, so no sample is generated by a stale policy.  
15. As a trainer running **off-policy**, I keep sending requests during the transition and rely on **the served checkpoint identity being tagged per token in every inference response**, so I can attribute each sample to the policy that produced it. *(Ask, section 6.7.)*  
16. As a trainer, I choose the **transition mode** per hot-load:  
    * async: freeze in-flight requests, pause new ones until the update completes.  
    * sync: drain in-flight requests, and have new ones **fast-rejected with HTTP 425 Too Early** so my client can back off deterministically instead of blocking on a queue. *(Ask, section 6.6.)*  
17. As a trainer, I control **prompt cache reset scope** (all, new\_session, none) across a weight change, so I do not serve tokens from a cache produced by different weights unless I explicitly allow it.  
    * In all modes, in-flight requests resume on their retained KV cache without recomputation. The reset scope governs requests admitted after the update:  
    * all: every new request recomputes its KV cache under the new weights, whether it continues an existing trajectory or starts a new one.  
    * new\_session: new requests continuing an existing trajectory session may reuse the old KV cache; requests starting a new trajectory always recompute.  
    * none: all new requests may reuse the old KV cache.  
18. As a trainer, I can **cancel a stuck hot-load** and read the **history** of past hot-loads for a deployment, so a bad round is recoverable and auditable.  
19. As a trainer, if a replica dies mid-run it is **replaced and comes back at the current checkpoint**, not at the base model, so the deployment never silently regresses to stale weights.  
20. As a trainer, I can increase the number of replicas and **new replicas should be brought up at the current latest checkpoint**, not at the base model, so the deployment never silently regresses to stale weights.

# 6\. Asks to NVIDIA

We are asking NVIDIA to close six gaps, in the priority order below. Items 1 to 3 are the critical enablers for large-scale RL. For each item, we need confirmation of the supported or planned approach, the owning component, and the delivery timeline.

### P0 Feature Requests

| Ask | Required outcome and current gap | Status |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |

| **6.1 Worker-to-worker GPU full weight transfer for delta weight revisions** | The first worker loads a full or delta checkpoint from object storage and reconstructs it locally when needed. ### P1 Feature Requests

These are about runtime and API contracts.

| Ask | Required outcome and current gap | Status |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **6.5 SGLang parity for RL routes** | Expose one per-replica RL contract across vLLM and SGLang. Today only vLLM registers /engine/\<route\> handlers and appears in GET /v1/rl/workers. | Rejected. NVIDIA stated that this is not in their goal as each engine has very specific implementation, no common standard. So VLLM and SGLANG backends will require different routes to actuate hotloads |
| **6.6 HTTP 425 during sync transitions** | Have the Dynamo router fast-reject new requests with **425 Too Early** while the selected engine is paused, instead of queueing them through a multi-minute update. |  |
| **6.2 Quantization during weight load** | Accept training-precision checkpoints and quantize them to the configured serving precision during hot-load. | Rejected. CoreWeave (or customer trainer) will own this part. Follow-up: Fuyuan to share examples w/ NVIDIA |
| **6.3 Efficient experience transfer for large training** | Provides efficient solutions to make the inference metadata required for training (completion\_token\_ids, prompt\_logprobs, logprobs, and routed\_experts) available to the external trainers, so large-batch rollout time is not bottlenecked. | Investigating |
